timeline:
COLD START (Horus not running), measured on this machine with materialsx-core-3 restored (2621 tracked files, 369122 gitignored paths), opening a 2-file PR. Wall clock from `open horus://review?url=...`:

0 ms — Raycast `open-in-horus` runs execFileAsync('open',[deepLink]) — extensions/horus/src/lib/horus.ts:15 (awaits the child's exit, ~70-110 ms).
111 ms — LaunchServices execs ~/Applications/Horus.app/Contents/MacOS/Horus (measured).
485 ms — main bundle top-level evaluated: process.title set — src/main/index.ts:103. findHorusReviewRequest(process.argv) queues the review — src/main/index.ts:208-209.
700 ms — app.whenReady: sync loadSessionState + loadWorkspaceCache (readFileSync + JSON.parse of last-workspace.json, 194 KB here / 1.9 MB on the user's other repo) — src/main/index.ts:995-996; registerIpcHandlers(); createMainWindow() → loadWindowState (sync) + window.show() via tryReveal — src/main/index.ts:1002-1005, src/main/windowReveal.ts:34-42. THE WINDOW IS ON SCREEN HERE — the reveal waits on nothing.
700 ms — applyExternalReview — src/main/index.ts:181-188: sets pendingOpenPullRequestUrl, revealMainWindow() (sync show+focus), publishPendingOpenPullRequest() → SKIPPED because webContents.isLoadingMainFrame() is true (src/main/index.ts:153); the renderer recovers it via did-finish-load (427-430) and its own getPendingExternalPullRequest poll (src/renderer/src/App.tsx:768-770), so nothing is lost. Then `void warmupPullRequest(url)`.
700 ms — warmupPullRequest → findPullRequestRoot → `await folderIndex.list(approvedRoots)` FIRST (src/main/index.ts:515) = ~/Developer walk, 88 readdir + 476 stat, 27 ms warm / 45 ms cold. The remembered root is only read afterwards (src/main/index.ts:517).
730 ms — first wave of 8 concurrent `git remote -v` — src/main/pullRequestRoots.ts:57-65 via remotesForRoot (src/main/index.ts:507-512). 13-18 spawns in total, because three separate resolutions each build their own remotesCache.
805 ms — renderer process starts. beginSessionRestore() → startLiveRefresh → RepositoryService.refresh() → `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z -- . <54 exclude pathspecs>` #1 — src/main/repository.ts:1341-1354.
805-1244 ms — THREE more identical ignored-file walks spawned (pids 81358/81460/81627/81660 observed), from openRepository()'s `void repositorySessions.refreshActive()` (src/main/index.ts:492-496) called once by warmupPullRequest and once by the renderer's resolvePullRequestRepository, plus the session restore. All four exit at 9336 ms.
943 ms — `gh pr view <url> --json <17 fields>,statusCheckRollup,mergeable` AND `gh api user --jq .login` start in parallel — src/main/repository.ts:2206-2215.
1264 ms — renderer first-contentful-paint.
1998 ms — `gh pr diff <url> --color never` starts — src/main/repository.ts:2314-2319. The metadata gate cost ~1055 ms.
1783-3000 ms — `.multi-file-review` first present in the DOM (1783 ms measured for a cache-hit PR launched directly, without the `open` hop).
2989 ms — patch in hand. `gh pr view --json number,url` spawned AGAIN by #resolvePullRequestIdentity — src/main/repository.ts:1823-1827 — duplicating owner/name/number already in review.pullRequest.url.
3475 ms — `gh api graphql --input -` for review threads — src/main/repository.ts:1794-1803.
9336 ms — the four ignored-file walks finally exit. CPU/IO saturated for the whole 9 s.

WARM (Horus already running; open-url delivered to the live instance, no second process):
0 ms — `open horus://...`; 68 ms — open-url delivered.
107-217 ms — new-tab pill "#NNN · owner/repo" visible in the titlebar (setNewWorldPending — src/renderer/src/useReviewWorlds.ts:659-665). This part is genuinely instant.
251-433 ms — 6-18 `git remote -v` spawns (three concurrent findPullRequestRoot calls).
326-507 ms — TWO concurrent ignored-file walks; they run for 7.0-8.4 s.
326-507 ms — `gh pr view` starts.
1413-1604 ms — `gh pr diff` starts (metadata gate 1.09-1.24 s).
1439 ms — DIFF VISIBLE when the PR is in the on-disk cache (PR 711, 138 files; PR 715, 126 files → 1667 ms).
2054 ms — DIFF VISIBLE for an uncached 1-file PR (#714); ~2660 ms for #713. Nothing is drawn at metadata time, because the warmup stole the review flight and with it the onProgress stream.

Renderer-internal (CDP, cold, launched via argv so no `open` hop): timeOrigin +459 ms from exec; renderer-loaded +619 ms; first-paint +619 ms; react-committed +703 ms; FCP +835 ms; .multi-file-review +1783 ms. Main-process IPC round trip during the open never exceeded 30 ms across 484 samples, and the renderer recorded zero longtasks for a 10-file PR and one 285 ms dropped frame for a 138-file PR — so the jank is (a) ~2 s of nothing on screen and (b) a single burst parse of the whole patch, not a blocked main loop.

findings.title: The on-disk PR cache cannot be read until a network `gh pr view` returns, so even a fully cached PR costs ~0.7-1.3 s before anything paints
findings.mechanism: PullRequestReviewCache keys entries on (url, headRefOid) — src/main/repository.ts:1034-1037, 1049-1050. headRefOid only exists after `gh pr view --json ...,headRefOid` completes (src/main/repository.ts:2206-2213), so #loadPullRequestReview always pays a full GitHub round trip before it may even look at disk. There is no URL-only index and no stale-while-revalidate path.
findings.evidence: Measured in ~/Developer/materialx/materialsx-core-3: `gh pr view 717 --json <17 fields>,statusCheckRollup,mergeable` = 720/687/853 ms; without the check fields = 616/787 ms. End-to-end, PR #715 (126 files) was already in ~/Library/Application Support/Horus/pr-cache and still took 1667 ms from `open horus://...` to `.multi-file-review` in the DOM; PR #711 (138 files, cached) took 1439 ms. No `gh pr diff` was spawned in either — the whole 1.4-1.7 s was the metadata round trip plus process/IPC overhead.
findings.fix: Add a URL-keyed index beside the oid-keyed entries: write `<sha1(url)>.latest.json` holding {headRefOid, pullRequestSummary, writtenAt} in PullRequestReviewCache.write (src/main/repository.ts:1077-1109). In #loadPullRequestReview, before spawning gh, read that index; if present, emit onProgress({kind:'metadata', review}) built from the cached summary plus the cached files/patch so the renderer paints immediately. Then run `gh pr view` in the background: if headRefOid matches, do nothing; if it differs, fetch the new diff and emit a replace. The PullRequestSummary is currently discarded by the cache and must be stored so the header can render from cache too.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 700-1250 ms on every re-open of a PR whose head has not moved (the common Cmd+H case after a warmup)

findings.title: warmupPullRequest steals the review flight and silently disables progressive rendering for the real open
findings.mechanism: applyExternalReview (src/main/index.ts:181-188) calls publishPendingOpenPullRequest() and then `void warmupPullRequest(url)`. warmupPullRequest calls `getPullRequestReview(url, undefined, `warmup:${url}`)` (src/main/index.ts:169) with NO onProgress. getPullRequestReview does `const inFlight = this.#reviewFlights.get(normalized); if (inFlight != null) return inFlight` (src/main/repository.ts:2183-2184) — the second caller's onProgress is discarded entirely. The renderer's call arrives later (it must cross IPC for resolvePullRequestRepository and activateRepository first — src/renderer/src/useGitWorkflow.ts:503-515), so it always joins the warmup's flight. Consequence: the renderer never receives the {kind:'metadata'} event that calls openPatchWorld and puts the review shell on screen (src/renderer/src/useGitWorkflow.ts:396-409), never receives {kind:'files'} pages (src/renderer/src/useGitWorkflow.ts:418), `streamed` stays false, and the whole review arrives as one IPC reply parsed in a single synchronous useMemo (src/renderer/src/useReviewLoadState.ts:257-305).
findings.evidence: Only ONE `gh pr view --json <full fields>` process is ever spawned per Cmd+H (process trace), proving the dedupe fires. For uncached PR #714 `gh pr view` returned at ~1.2 s but `.multi-file-review` only appeared at 2054 ms — after `gh pr diff` finished — instead of at metadata time. For uncached #713 the trace shows `gh pr view` at 363 ms, `gh pr diff` at 1604 ms, identity call at 2659 ms, with no intermediate paint. A 138-file PR produced a single 285 ms dropped frame (rAF sampling over CDP) when the whole patch landed at once; a 10-file PR produced zero longtasks.
findings.fix: Make the flight multicast instead of first-writer-wins. Replace `#reviewFlights: Map<string, Promise<PullRequestReview>>` with `Map<string, {promise, listeners: Set<(p: PullRequestReviewProgress) => void>, metadata: PullRequestReviewProgress | null}>`. In getPullRequestReview (src/main/repository.ts:2176-2196): when a flight exists, add the caller's onProgress to `listeners`, immediately replay the stored metadata event to it, and return the promise. Have #loadPullRequestReview fan every onProgress?.(...) call (src/main/repository.ts:2245, 2273-2279, 2296) out to all listeners and remember the metadata event. Cheaper stopgap: skip the warmup when intent === 'open' (src/main/index.ts:187) — the renderer's own request is only 30-80 ms behind and it does stream.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 800-1000 ms to first visible content on an uncached PR (shell at metadata time rather than after the diff), plus removal of a 285 ms+ single-burst parse that scales with patch size

findings.title: Every Cmd+H fires 2-4 concurrent full-worktree `git ls-files --others --ignored` walks that saturate CPU and IO for 7-9 s
findings.line: 1341-1354 (the three-way Promise.all in refresh()); triggered from src/main/index.ts:492-496 and 1007
findings.mechanism: RepositoryService.refresh() always runs the gitignored-file walk in parallel with `ls-files --cached` and `status`. The GIT_IGNORED_EXCLUSION_PATHSPECS (src/main/repository.ts:323-326) filter git's OUTPUT; git still stats every ignored path. There is no in-flight dedupe on refresh(), and openRepository (src/main/index.ts:477-498) fires `void repositorySessions.refreshActive()` on the cache-hydrate path every time it is called. On a Cmd+H it is called once by warmupPullRequest (src/main/index.ts:168) and once by the renderer's resolvePullRequestRepository (src/main/index.ts:585); on a cold start beginSessionRestore (src/main/index.ts:1007 → 967-979) adds a third and repositorySessions.open/#refreshAndPublish (src/main/repositorySessions.ts:157, 200-208) a fourth.
findings.evidence: `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z -- . <exclusions>` in materialsx-core-3, standalone: real 1.88 s, user 0.39 s, sys 1.47 s; the unfiltered walk enumerates 369,122 ignored paths. Cold Cmd+H process trace shows four such children (pids 81358, 81460, 81627, 81660) alive from 805 ms to 9336 ms. Warm Cmd+H shows two, alive 326→7372 ms and 507→8364 ms. By contrast `ls-files --cached` = 63 ms and `status --porcelain=v2 -uall` = 618 ms.
findings.fix: Three independent cheap changes: (1) add in-flight dedupe to RepositoryService.refresh() — keep `#refreshFlight: Promise<RepositorySnapshot> | null` and return it while a refresh is running (src/main/repository.ts:1334). (2) Split the ignored walk out of refresh(): return the snapshot from `ls-files --cached` + `status` (618 ms combined) and merge the ignored set in a second, debounced pass that only runs when the Explorer actually shows ignored files. (3) Pass a flag through openRepository(root, activate=false) that skips the ignored walk entirely on the PR-open path — a PR review never reads the ignored set. If the walk must stay, replace the 54 exclude pathspecs with `--directory` plus a post-filter, or enumerate with the already-bundled ripgrep (RIPGREP_EXECUTABLE, src/main/repository.ts:349), which honours .gitignore natively and does not stat inside ignored directories.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Removes 7-9 s of background CPU/IO saturation per Cmd+H (~3-6 CPU-seconds, mostly sys). The main contributor to the 'janky all over the place' feel and to battery drain

findings.title: Three independent findPullRequestRoot() resolutions run concurrently per Cmd+H, each with its own remotes cache
findings.mechanism: warmupPullRequest (src/main/index.ts:166), the renderer's resolvePullRequestRepository (src/renderer/src/useGitWorkflow.ts:503 → src/main/index.ts:582) and previewPullRequestFolder (src/renderer/src/useGitWorkflow.ts:153-173 → src/main/index.ts:559) all call findPullRequestRoot for the same URL at the same time. findMatchingPullRequestRoot builds a fresh `remotesCache` per invocation (src/main/pullRequestRoots.ts:17-24), so `git remote -v` is respawned for every candidate root in every pass. remotesForRoot also adds a `stat` per root (src/main/index.ts:508). There is no shared promise, no negative cache, and no memo of the resolved root for the duration of the open.
findings.evidence: Process traces show 13 `git` children at t=433 ms and 18 at t=251 ms on a machine with only 6 approvedRoots — the 6-root preferred wave run two to three times. Measured `git remote -v` spawn = 10-20 ms. Worst case measured: probing all 103 candidate folders under ~/Developer in waves of 8 costs 456 ms and 103 spawns; times three concurrent resolutions that is ~309 spawns whenever the PR's repo is not already an approved root.
findings.fix: Add a module-level `const rootResolutions = new Map<string, Promise<string | null>>()` in src/main/index.ts and wrap findPullRequestRoot so all three callers share one promise per URL (delete on settle, or keep for a short TTL). Additionally hoist the remotes cache out of findMatchingPullRequestRoot into a module-level `Map<root, {remotes, expiresAt}>` with a ~60 s TTL — a repository's remotes essentially never change during a session.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 100-400 ms typical; up to ~900 ms and ~200 fewer process spawns when the PR's repo is not in approvedRoots

findings.title: findPullRequestRoot awaits the whole ~/Developer folder walk before it looks at the remembered root — a regression against the committed version
findings.mechanism: Line 515 is `const catalog = await folderIndex.list(sessionState.approvedRoots)`; the remembered root is only read on line 517, and the open sessions / approvedRoots only reach findMatchingPullRequestRoot afterwards. The walk therefore gates the fast path it was meant to back up. FolderIndex caches for 30 s (src/main/folderIndex.ts:31, 112-125), so any two Cmd+H presses more than 30 s apart both pay for it.
findings.evidence: `git diff HEAD -- src/main/index.ts` shows the committed findPullRequestRoot probed only `[...repositorySessions.roots, ...sessionState.approvedRoots]` in a single Promise.all, with no folder walk and no wave batching. Replicating collectFolderCandidates with bun: 103 folders, 88 readdir + 476 stat, 27 ms warm (45 ms per the lead's cold run). The installed build at ~/Applications/Horus.app contains this code — its minified findPullRequestRoot (`We`) awaits `Rt.list(b.approvedRoots)` before calling the matcher — so the user is running the regressed path. last-session.json now contains pullRequestFolders {'fehrmann-materialsx/materialsx-core': '.../materialsx-core-3'}, so the remembered root exists and is being skipped past.
findings.fix: Restructure findPullRequestRoot into two stages: stage 1 probes `[remembered, ...repositorySessions.roots, ...sessionState.approvedRoots]` in one Promise.all (no waves, no folder walk) and returns on the first match; stage 2 (only on a miss) awaits folderIndex.list() and runs the existing name-biased wave scan. Keep findMatchingPullRequestRoot for stage 2 and pass it `preferredRoots: []`.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 27-45 ms on this machine on every PR open; unbounded (hundreds of ms to seconds) on a machine with a large or network-backed ~/Developer, and it removes the walk from the path entirely for a remembered repo

findings.title: previewPullRequestFolder runs a full root resolution purely to label a chip in the titlebar
findings.mechanism: openPullRequestFromLocator calls updateNewWorldLocator (src/renderer/src/useGitWorkflow.ts:497), which makes the effect at src/renderer/src/useGitWorkflow.ts:153-173 fire (newWorldId != null, newWorldRoot == null, locator is a PR URL). It invokes window.repository.previewPullRequestFolder, which in main runs the full findPullRequestRoot — folder walk plus up to 400 `git remote -v` spawns — and the result is consumed only by reviewFolderChip (src/renderer/src/pullRequestOpen.ts:5-17) to render a folder name and path next to the locator.
findings.evidence: src/main/index.ts:559 `const root = await findPullRequestRoot(pullRequestUrl)` inside previewPullRequestFolder; its return value is {root, name, displayPath, source} — display data only. IPC handler registered at src/main/index.ts:683-684. This is the third of the three concurrent resolutions counted in PR-4 (13-18 `git remote -v` spawns observed).
findings.fix: Make previewPullRequestFolder cheap and non-probing: look up rememberedPullRequestFolder(sessionState, slug) (src/main/sessionStore.ts:46-48), stat it, and return it with source:'remembered'; return null when there is no memory. Do not walk and do not spawn git. If a chip for an unremembered repo is wanted, have it join the shared resolution promise from PR-4 instead of starting a new one.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Removes one of three concurrent resolutions: ~30-150 ms of contention typically, ~450 ms and ~103 git spawns when the repo is unknown

findings.title: The large-PR fallback re-fetches metadata it already has, costing an extra ~700 ms `gh pr view`
findings.mechanism: When `gh pr diff` returns HTTP 406 (GitHub refuses diffs over 20000 lines / 300 files), #collectPullRequestPatch falls through to the files API (src/main/repository.ts:2333). That path calls #resolvePullRequestIdentity, which spawns `gh pr view <selector> --json number,url` to learn owner/name/number — values already parsed into `pullRequest.url` and `pullRequest.number` a few lines earlier at src/main/repository.ts:2216-2222. The same duplication hits getPullRequestConversation (src/main/repository.ts:1793), which is what the user pays right after the diff lands.
findings.evidence: `gh pr diff 715` fails after 1045 ms with 'HTTP 406: Sorry, the diff exceeded the maximum number of lines (20000)'. `gh pr view 715 --json number,url` = ~700 ms. One wave of 8 concurrent `gh api .../pulls/715/files?per_page=100&page=N` = 853 ms; a single page = 839-1044 ms. In the cold trace the identity call appears at 2989 ms and the graphql call at 3475 ms.
findings.fix: In #loadPullRequestReview, right after parsing `details`, seed the identity cache: `this.#pullRequestIdentities.set(normalizedSelector, {owner, name, number})` derived from pullRequest.url via githubRepoSlugFromRemoteUrl (src/main/repository.ts:1830) and pullRequest.number. Also start the files-API paging concurrently with `gh pr diff` when `details.changedFiles > 300`, instead of waiting for the 406.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~700 ms on every PR over 300 files, and ~700 ms off the conversation fetch on every PR

findings.title: `gh pr diff` costs ~1 s even for a one-file PR and is a strictly serial second hop after metadata
findings.mechanism: #collectPullRequestPatch only starts after the metadata await at src/main/repository.ts:2206-2215 resolves, because the cache probe (2247) sits between them. The two round trips are serial even though the diff request does not need headRefOid.
findings.evidence: `gh pr diff 717 --color never` (2 files, 166 lines) = 1211/1242/1060 ms; `gh pr diff 716` (16 files, 64 KB) = 1220 ms. Cold trace: `gh pr view` at 943 ms, `gh pr diff` at 1998 ms, done ~2989 ms — two serial ~1 s hops.
findings.fix: Start `gh pr diff` immediately, in parallel with `gh pr view`, and race it against the cache probe: if the cache hits on the returned headRefOid, abort the diff child through the existing AbortSignal (src/main/repository.ts:2189; runCommand already accepts `signal` — src/main/gitCommands.ts:261, 276). Worst case one wasted `gh` process; best case the two ~1 s hops collapse into one.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~900-1100 ms on an uncached PR open

findings.title: The optional check fields make the blocking metadata call measurably slower
findings.mechanism: #runPullRequestJsonCommand always appends `statusCheckRollup,mergeable` to the 17 review fields. Those two make `gh pr view` resolve extra GraphQL connections; nothing in the diff rendering path needs them — they only feed PullRequestChecks (src/main/repository.ts:779-797). The `files` field in PULL_REQUEST_REVIEW_FIELDS (src/main/repository.ts:155) is likewise fetched and then only used for a Math.max on expectedFileCount (src/main/repository.ts:2225-2231).
findings.evidence: Measured on PR 717 in materialsx-core-3: with check fields 720/687/853 ms; without them 616/787 ms.
findings.fix: Split the metadata call: fetch PULL_REQUEST_LIST_FIELDS + baseRefOid + headRefOid (drop `files`, `statusCheckRollup`, `mergeable`) on the open path, emit the metadata progress event, and fetch checks in a second background `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup,mergeable` that patches the header when it lands.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 60-170 ms on every PR open, on the strictly blocking hop

findings.title: A Cmd+H cold start renders the whole restored desk workspace before the PR world, and may load the wrong viewer chunk
findings.mechanism: mountApp AWAITS `preloadWorkspaceRoot()` (WorkspaceRoot-*.js, 269 KB) and `preloadWorkspaceViewer(cachedPaint.workspaceView)` before createRoot().render() whenever a cached workspace exists. On a Cmd+H launch the cached view is whatever the user last had — if it resolves to the single-file surface, DiffSurface is loaded and MultiFileReview-*.js (103 KB) is only fetched later by the effect at src/renderer/src/RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:874-879. The renderer also fully hydrates the 3026-path explorer and the last file's comparison, all of which is replaced a second later by the PR world (src/renderer/src/useReviewWorlds.ts:705-735).
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/boot.tsx:21-24 is an `await Promise.all([...])` in front of the render. out/renderer/assets: boot-*.js 439 KB, boot-*.css 172 KB, WorkspaceRoot-*.js 269 KB, MultiFileReview-*.js 103 KB. Measured renderer milestones on a cold PR launch: renderer-loaded +149 ms, react-committed +244 ms, FCP +376 ms relative to a timeOrigin that is itself +459 ms from exec. A restore-only launch probed over CDP showed #repository-diff (DiffSurface) rendered, not .multi-file-review.
findings.fix: Expose the pending external PR URL to the preload synchronously — main knows it before createMainWindow (src/main/index.ts:999-1006), and additionalArguments already carries encodeRestoreHintArgument(currentRestoreHint()) at src/main/index.ts:332, so adding a field costs nothing. In boot.tsx, when that field is set: skip the desk `await` entirely, preload MultiFileReview instead of the cached view's chunk, and render immediately; keep WorkspaceRoot preloading in the background.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 150-400 ms to the review shell on a cold Cmd+H, and it removes a full explorer + file-diff render that is thrown away

findings.title: pendingOpenPullRequestUrl is never cleared, so a renderer reload silently reopens the last external PR
findings.mechanism: applyExternalReview assigns pendingOpenPullRequestUrl (src/main/index.ts:183) and nothing ever resets it. publishPendingOpenPullRequest is re-run from the did-finish-load handler (src/main/index.ts:427-430) on every document load, and the getPendingExternalPullRequest handler (src/main/index.ts:687) keeps answering with it. The renderer's only guard is a closure variable `opened` (src/renderer/src/App.tsx:761-766), recreated on every mount, so it does not survive a reload. scheduleRecovery reloads the renderer on a crash or load failure (src/main/index.ts:354-372, 438-449).
findings.evidence: src/main/index.ts:132 `let pendingOpenPullRequestUrl: string | null = null`, with the only write at line 183; grep finds no reset. src/renderer/src/App.tsx:758-772 registers the listener and polls getPendingExternalPullRequest inside `useEffect(..., [])`.
findings.fix: Clear pendingOpenPullRequestUrl once the renderer has taken it: null it inside the getPendingExternalPullRequest handler (src/main/index.ts:687) after returning, or add an ack channel the renderer calls from the `open` callback in src/renderer/src/App.tsx:762-766.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0 ms steady state; avoids an unwanted full PR fetch (~2 s plus network and gh rate budget) after every renderer recovery

findings.title: Two independent clipboard warmups run forever, and a PR with no local checkout re-probes every folder each time with no negative cache
findings.mechanism: startClipboardWarmup polls clipboard.readText() on the main thread every CLIPBOARD_WARMUP_MS = 800 ms (src/main/index.ts:71, 199-205) for the life of the process and calls warmupPullRequest on any new PR URL. Separately the Raycast `warmup-clipboard` command runs on a 10 s interval and fires `open -g horus://...&intent=warmup` (extensions/horus/src/warmup-clipboard.ts:8-29), which will launch Horus in the background if it is not running. warmupPullRequest's cooldown map (src/main/index.ts:135, 161-162, 170) is only populated on SUCCESS, so a URL whose repository has no local checkout — findPullRequestRoot returns null at src/main/index.ts:167 — is re-probed in full (folder walk + up to 103 `git remote -v`) every time the clipboard changes back to it.
findings.evidence: src/main/index.ts:170 `recentlyWarmedAt.set(url, Date.now())` sits after the `if (matchingRoot == null) return` on line 167. Measured full-candidate probe: 456 ms, 103 git spawns. The Raycast command's own dedupe is a Raycast Cache keyed on the URL (extensions/horus/src/warmup-clipboard.ts:17) and does not cover the in-app poller.
findings.fix: Record the attempt regardless of outcome — move `recentlyWarmedAt.set(url, Date.now())` above the null check, or add a `noLocalCheckout: Set<slug>` consulted by findPullRequestRoot. Raise CLIPBOARD_WARMUP_MS to 2500 ms and skip the poll while the window is hidden or unfocused. Since the Raycast extension already polls every 10 s, consider deleting the in-app poller entirely.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Removes a repeating 450 ms / 103-spawn burst for unmatched URLs and ~4300 main-thread wakeups per hour

findings.title: The Raycast fallback branch is a silent no-op when Horus is already running, and the primary branch awaits the `open` child
findings.mechanism: sendToHorus awaits `execFileAsync('open', [deepLink])` and, on any non-zero exit, retries with `open -a Horus --args --horus-url=...`. On macOS `open -a` against an already-running application activates it and discards `--args`, so the fallback reports success while delivering nothing — Horus comes forward with no PR. When the fallback does fire on a cold app it adds a second LaunchServices dispatch. The await also holds the Raycast command open for the duration of the `open` child.
findings.evidence: Measured LaunchServices dispatch: 111 ms cold (main process exec at t=111 ms in the process trace), 68 ms warm. extensions/horus/src/lib/horus.ts:15 and 17-21 as written. `if (app.isPackaged) app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient(HORUS_PROTOCOL)` (src/main/index.ts:216) means a `bun run dev` build never registers the scheme — exactly when the fallback would be exercised.
findings.fix: Detect the running instance first (`pgrep -x Horus`) and, when it is running, only use the horus:// form; when it is not, `open -a Horus --args --horus-url=...` is correct. Do not await the child — fire and forget after closeMainWindow, since a failure cannot be surfaced once the Raycast window has closed. Show a distinct HUD when the scheme is unregistered instead of falling through to a branch that cannot work.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 70-110 ms when the fallback fires; removes a silent-failure mode

findings.title: cancelPullRequestReview(requestId) at the top of getPullRequestReview is dead code, so an older review of a different PR is never cancelled
findings.mechanism: `this.cancelPullRequestReview(requestId)` is called with the id of the request being created, before its AbortController is registered on line 2188. #reviewAborts never contains that key yet, so the call aborts nothing. Because #reviewFlights is keyed by normalized selector, opening PR B while PR A is still downloading leaves A's `gh` children running to completion — the exact waste the comment at src/main/repository.ts:2163-2165 says it is guarding against.
findings.evidence: src/main/repository.ts:2186-2188 in order: cancelPullRequestReview(requestId); const abort = new AbortController(); this.#reviewAborts.set(requestId, abort). The only other cancellation entry point is the cancelPullRequestReview IPC (src/main/index.ts:738-741), which the renderer calls on world close.
findings.fix: Either delete line 2186 as misleading, or make it cancel the right thing: track the current foreground request id per repository and abort that one when a new foreground (non-warmup) request arrives, leaving warmup flights alone.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0 ms on the happy path; frees up to 8 concurrent `gh api` children and their rate-limit budget when the user opens a second PR mid-download

findings.title: scripts/benchmark-startup.mjs fails for a stale reason, not a slow startup — it waits for a review surface a plain restore never renders
findings.mechanism: The loop only breaks once BOTH `#repository-explorer` and `.multi-file-review, .multi-file-code-view` exist. On a plain restore the workspace opens the single-file surface (`#repository-diff` / DiffSurface) whenever the remembered selectedPath is not one of the changed files, because the view is recomputed from the tree path (src/renderer/src/workspaceMode.ts:19-26) rather than taken from the cached 'multi'. The review selectors therefore never appear and the run throws regardless of how fast startup was.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: `HORUS_STARTUP_SAMPLES=1 HORUS_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS=15000 bun run scripts/benchmark-startup.mjs` still throws 'The restored explorer and review surface did not become usable.' at 15 s. Launching identically (`open -na ~/Applications/Horus.app --args --remote-debugging-port=9470`) and probing over CDP after 6 s gives {explorer:true, review:false, mfcv:false, diffPanel:true} with body text 'materialsx-core-3 / 419 MB / dev / 3,026 files / ... test_heatmap_service.py'. Marks: renderer-loaded 256 ms, viewer-committed 338 ms, explorer-committed 338 ms, react-committed 354 ms — startup is fast. last-workspace.json has workspaceView 'multi' but selectedPath 'apps/aim2-backend/tests/test_heatmap_service.py', which is not among the 12 statuses. All three selectors do exist in the codebase (src/renderer/src/Explorer.tsx:120, src/renderer/src/MultiFileReview.tsx:898, src/renderer/src/styles.css:1167).
findings.fix: Wait for whichever viewer the restore actually produces: change the review probe to `document.querySelector('.multi-file-review, .multi-file-code-view, #repository-diff') != null`, or have the benchmark force the review view (select a changed file, or drive the deep link) before measuring. Until then the harness cannot regression-test startup at all.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0 ms of app latency; unblocks the only automated startup regression gate

openQuestions: Is the ~2 s the user calls 'slow' dominated by the two serial gh round trips (PR-1/PR-8) or by the ignored-file walks (PR-3)? The IPC-lag probe (max 30 ms over 484 samples) and the longtask probe (0 longtasks for a 10-file PR) say the main loop and the renderer are both idle during those 2 s, so on materialsx-core-3 it is the network. On the user's other repo (20k paths, 1.9 MB workspace cache) the walks may also block — the same two probes should be re-run there.

How large is the user's typical PR? The single-burst parse caused by PR-2 was only 285 ms at 138 files here; at the 3000-file ceiling (MAX_PULL_REQUEST_FILES, src/main/patchBuilder.ts:16) the same burst would be seconds. The size distribution decides whether PR-2 is purely a latency fix or also the main jank fix.

Is `gh pr view --json headRefOid` alone materially faster than the 17-field request? Not measured separately. If it is, it becomes the cheap background revalidation call for the cache-first design in PR-1.

MAX_PULL_REQUEST_CACHE_ENTRIES is 20 (src/main/repository.ts:134) while the byte cap is 200 MB and the directory holds only 4.9 MB — the entry count is what evicts. Should the count cap be raised so a day of Cmd+H reviews stays cached, given PR-1 makes cache hits the fast path?

Every Cmd+H opens a new world/tab (src/renderer/src/useReviewWorlds.ts:705-735) and tabs accumulate without bound; only patch payloads past 64 MB are released (src/renderer/src/useReviewWorlds.ts:132, 293-337) and up to 3 CodeView instances stay mounted (src/renderer/src/worldViewCache.ts:18). Whether that contributes to the 'janky all over the place' feel over a long session was not measured — it needs a multi-hour profile.

Should the Raycast `warmup-clipboard` 10 s background command exist at all now that main polls the clipboard itself every 800 ms (src/main/index.ts:199-205)? Keeping both means the app can be launched in the background by a clipboard change the user never acted on.
